metadata.title: Survey of Adult Skills – Reader’s Companion (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This Reader’s Companion documents how the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 is designed and how results are reported, including survey paths, sampling frames, exclusions, and quality checks. It explains that proficiency results are disseminated as average proficiency scores and shares at proficiency levels, which in PIAAC-style reporting relies on the survey’s weighting and scaling approach to represent the target adult population within participating countries/economies. The document also notes that alternative weighting schemes and non-response bias analyses are part of the quality assurance process, but it does not provide a specific weight variable name in the excerpt provided. Because this is a methodological companion rather than an empirical ML analysis paper, the exact application of student weights/replicate weights in any downstream modeling is not specified here; analysts should consult the forthcoming Survey of Adult Skills 2023 Technical Report for the precise weighting and replicate-weight procedures.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a reader’s companion describing what the Survey of Adult Skills measures and how results are reported, rather than presenting an empirical model that uses PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes. As such, plausible-value generation/combination and missing-data handling strategies for an analysis model are not specified in the provided text. The companion points readers to a forthcoming technical report for more technically oriented methodological details, so the PV and missing-data procedures are not reported at the level required for extraction here.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This Reader’s Companion describes the overall survey design and implementation for the 2023 Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC), including sampling frames (population registry vs screeners), exclusions from the target population, survey paths, and achieved response rates. However, the provided excerpt does not include the numeric analytic sample size (N) or per-country/economy sample counts, nor does it specify a particular analytic subsample restriction (e.g., only certain survey paths or modules) for an empirical analysis.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Reader’s Companion explains the “what” and “how” of the 2023 Survey of Adult Skills, a product of the OECD Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC). It focuses on three cognitive information-processing domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—and describes how results are disseminated using average proficiency scores and proficiency levels (i.e., what different scores/levels mean in terms of expected capabilities). The document also outlines the role of an extensive background questionnaire and discusses how social and emotional skills are measured via BFI-2-S instruments, including standardisation choices for cross-country comparability. For survey design and data quality, it summarises key implementation aspects such as survey paths, sampling frames, exclusions, response rates, and non-response bias checks, while directing readers to a forthcoming technical report for more detailed methodological implementation.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a methodological/interpretive companion report rather than an empirical study estimating predictive models on microdata. Consequently, there is no student-level analytic sample size, no country-level N table in the provided excerpt, no ML algorithm evaluation, and no target-variable performance metrics to extract. The companion’s purpose is to document measurement domains, reporting conventions, and survey design/quality assurance, so fields related to PV handling in an analysis model and missing-data handling are not presented as extractable empirical-method parameters here.
